functions.name: kdrv_display_back_buffer
functions.why: MIPI-DSI + CO5300 AMOLED bring-up (esp_lcd_*, DPHY LDO, DSI host registers), DMA flush with an ISR-signalled completion semaphore, DCS brightness through the DSI command FIFO, LP-store recovery counter, pad holds across restart. (This function's own body makes no hardware call: it is an accessor/pure body, but the state it reads is produced by the other functions of this unit, so it still belongs in the fake.)
functions.contract: The framebuffer the next frame is assembled in, for a caller that draws whole frames itself. A renderer that produces the whole panel at once - a PPA scaling a game's frame, a video decoder - writes straight into this buffer and then flushes the whole panel with this pointer as its pixels, and... Returns: The back buffer, 410 x 502 RGB565 with a stride of 820 bytes in a KDRV_DISPLAY_FB_BYTES allocation, or NULL when the panel is not up or runs on a single framebuffer.
functions.bench: <canvas> of the device screen reading the framebuffer (page-side, per frame via kweb_state), brightness slider -> CSS filter, screenshot/capture buttons. Flush completion should be raised from the page frame callback (or immediately in the fake) on a pthread, never in a JS-only context.

functions.why: Hardware JPEG encoder (driver/jpeg_encode.h) for screenshots/mirror.
functions.contract: Compress a rectangle of RGB565 into JPEG. The INPUT needs no alignment - the driver imposes none, which is what lets a band of the panel's framebuffer be encoded where it lies instead of copied first. The OUTPUT does, and this file owns a buffer that satisfies it. Returns: KODE_DENIED before kdrv_jpeg_init(), for a NULL rgb565/out/out_len, for w or h of 0, for quality outside 1..100, or when another call is already encoding - the last is a normal, expected outcome under contention, not a fault. KODE_ERROR if the engine refused, KODE_NO_RESOURCES if the result did...

functions.contract: `test component=jpeg`: encode a known rectangle and read it back. Returns: KODE_OK if the SOI/EOI framing checks out, KODE_DENIED if the encoder was busy with someone else's call rather than broken - a caller should tell an operator to retry, not that the codec failed - KODE_ERROR or KODE_NO_RESOURCES otherwise.

functions.name: khal_console_dock_release
functions.why: USB-CDC (TinyUSB) / USB-serial-JTAG / UART console transport (driver_install, vfs, tinyusb_cdcacm_*): hardware transport.
functions.contract: Let the dock console's pins go: TinyUSB off the pads and the pads handed to the GPIO matrix, for a test that drives them itself. The cable console is untouched. Without the dock built in (CONFIG_KHAL_CONSOLE_DOCK off) nothing holds the pins and this does nothing. Returns: KODE_OK.
functions.bench: Terminal pane in the page (xterm-like) wired to the USB cable bench object: bytes typed -> reader callback; khal_console_write -> terminal output queue. Cable unplugged -> read blocks, write drops.

functions.name: khal_console_dock_take
functions.why: USB-CDC (TinyUSB) / USB-serial-JTAG / UART console transport (driver_install, vfs, tinyusb_cdcacm_*): hardware transport.
functions.contract: Put the dock console back on its pins after khal_console_dock_release(). The pins must be inputs again, their UART freed, before this is called. A dock already up, or none built in, is left as it is. Returns: KODE_OK; KODE_ERROR when TinyUSB would not install again, the cable console intact.
functions.bench: Terminal pane in the page (xterm-like) wired to the USB cable bench object: bytes typed -> reader callback; khal_console_write -> terminal output queue. Cable unplugged -> read blocks, write drops.

functions.bench: Terminal pane in the page (xterm-like) wired to the USB cable bench object: bytes typed -> reader callback; khal_console_write -> terminal output queue. Cable unplugged -> read blocks, write drops.

functions.name: khal_console_raw_begin
functions.why: USB-CDC (TinyUSB) / USB-serial-JTAG / UART console transport (driver_install, vfs, tinyusb_cdcacm_*): hardware transport. (This function's own body makes no hardware call: it is an accessor/pure body, but the state it reads is produced by the other functions of this unit, so it still belongs in the fake.)
functions.contract: Ask the reader task to call @p pump instead of reporting bytes. At its next pass the reader discards pending input, enters raw mode and calls @p on_armed. @p pump then runs on the reader task until it calls khal_console_raw_end(). Returns: KODE_OK; KODE_DENIED for a NULL argument or when raw mode is already armed or requested.
functions.bench: Terminal pane in the page (xterm-like) wired to the USB cable bench object: bytes typed -> reader callback; khal_console_write -> terminal output queue. Cable unplugged -> read blocks, write drops.

functions.contract: Tell the reader the board is asleep, or that it is not any more. The reader wakes about 200 times a second to look at the dock, and about 20 to look for a raw-mode request, which is a wake of the P4 every time. Asleep there is no host on either port (a cable never sleeps) and no verb to ask for...

units.why: The real driver is DSI/PPA/JPEG-engine code with ISR completion. kscreen (LVGL flush) and display_ao call only this API, and a flush that signals the semaphore from the page frame loop is enough. kdrv_compose_check.c (parameter checking) stays real.

contract_notes: Panel is 410x502 RGB565 (KBSP_LCD_H_RES x V_RES, stride 820 B; frame = 411640 B, cache-line aligned 64). kdrv_display_init blocks ~100 ms, once, from AO_Display. kdrv_display_flush(rect,pixels) returns as soon as the "DMA is queued"; completion is ONE signal per flush on the semaphore (kdrv_display_flush_wait(ms) returns false on timeout; kscreen then drops the frame, and display_ao waits on it forever otherwise) - flush_abort completes it without a transfer. A flush whose pixels are the front/back framebuffer flips buffers instead of copying. brightness 0..100 (0 = black), writes paced >= 2 frames. panel_sleep blocks ~120-160 ms. capture_begin returns a complete BMP of the glass; band(y,h) reads rows of the glass; dirty_take returns the changed row range then clears it. link_set(false/true) takes the DSI scan-out down/up with panel memory kept.

Pictures are ARGB/RGB565 with address and size multiples of KDRV_COMPOSE_ALIGN (64) and sides <= KDRV_COMPOSE_SIDE_MAX; PPA owner thread only (one pass at a time). blend: fg at opacity over dst; fill: 0xAARRGGBB; scale: scaled/rotated copy. Return KODE_* statuses per header; parameter validation lives in kdrv_compose_check.c (real, in SOURCES_UNDER_TEST) and can be kept.

kdrv_jpeg_encode(rgb565,w,h,quality,&out,&out_len) is synchronous and returns a driver-owned buffer (aligned output). Needed for `screenshot` and the mirror; may be implemented with a software encoder in wasm or by round-tripping through the page (canvas.toBlob) on a worker.
kdrv_ppa_prepare(src,w,h,scale 1|2,&dst,&dst_w,&dst_h) returns an RGB565 buffer (halved when scale=2) owned by the driver; one user at a time (guard).
